title: Defining Off-road Running: A Position Statement from the Ultra Sports Science Foundation
authors: Scheer V, Basset P, Giovanelli N, Vernillo G, Millet GP, Costa RJS
population: Position statement on terminology for off-road running events and athletes
findings: Ultramarathon running is defined as any running event over marathon distance conducted in any terrain and surface.
Trail, mountain, skyrunning, fell, orienteering, obstacle course and cross-country running overlap but have distinct features and need clear terminology.
It recommends describing events by distance, surface, elevation change and altitude, continuous vs staged format, type of support, name and year of the event, and governing body.
It recommends describing athletes by basic data, physiological determinants, and training and competition characteristics.
Trail, mountain, sky, fell running, orienteering, obstacle course and cross-country events are mostly off-road but have distinct features.
Ultramarathon is any event beyond marathon distance on any terrain.
Studies and reports should state distance, surface, elevation change and altitude, event type (continuous vs staged), support, event name/year and governing body.
Athletes should be described by basic data, physiological determinants, training and competition characteristics.
limitations: A terminology and reporting statement; no training prescription, outcome data or numeric thresholds.
implications: Model race goals with the statement's descriptors as fields: distance, elevation gain/loss, surface, altitude, continuous vs staged, support level, so plan rules can branch on them.
Treat 'ultramarathon' as any distance above 42.2 km, making 50 km the lower bound of the ultra module; no training parameter change is justified by this paper.
Define plan inputs for course goals with distance, total ascent and descent, altitude range and surface, as the statement recommends reporting.
Do not make an event-type-specific training rule from this paper.

verification.notes: Crossref (2020-02-14) and Europe PMC abstract re-fetched; claims confirmed. Evidence level downgraded from A to D: it is a consensus on terminology, not on training effects. Scheer et al. 2021 ultra-trail position statements were not found in Europe PMC searches in this session and are listed under gaps.
